reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.text:
I honestly never thought I’d be writing a review like this.

I’ve been using StrongLifts since the very beginning, back when it was essentially an email from Mehdi, long before there was even an app. I’ve been through the different versions, trials, and changes over the years. I even paid for a full year of the app at one point and customized my workouts to add additional exercises. I’ve logged thousands of workouts over the years and referred a bunch of people to use the app and follow the workout.

That’s why opening the app today and being told I’m essentially locked out unless I pay after a 7-day free trial was incredibly disappointing.

What made StrongLifts great to me was its simplicity. It wasn’t complicated, it didn’t try to be everything to everyone, and it made tracking workouts easy. I stuck with it for years because I genuinely liked it.

But after being a loyal user for so long, it’s frustrating to see what once felt like a great fitness tool become so heavily focused on monetization. I understand that apps need to make money, but there’s something especially disappointing about longtime users suddenly being treated like new customers who need to subscribe just to continue using something they’ve relied on for years.

The irony is that I can track my workouts for free using plenty of other methods. I stayed with StrongLifts because I liked StrongLifts, not because I couldn’t find another way to track a workout.

Or better yet, just use Claude to create a workout logging app for you.

In today’s day and age I don’t understand why anyone would even consider paying $11+/month for an app that does something as simple as logging a workout.

reviews.title: Deceptive “Lifetime” purchase.
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this app off and on for ten years, ever since I made the decision to pay upfront for a "lifetime pass" under the clear impression that I would have access to the service for as long as the app existed. It is incredibly disappointing to see the developer now unilaterally revoke that access and force long-term supporters into a monthly subscription model.

Selling a "lifetime" product is a contract of trust. By moving the goalposts and essentially nullifying the purchase I made a decade ago, the developer has shown a complete lack of respect for their early adopters. It feels like a total bait-and-switch; they got the initial influx of cash they needed to grow, and now that they have a steady user base, they’ve decided to squeeze those same people for recurring monthly fees.

I understand that development costs change, but if you cannot sustain your business model, the solution is not to steal from those who believed in you at the beginning. Very disappointed.

reviews.title: Forced into subscription, no free version anymore
reviews.text:
They’ve recently changed to for ing everyone to subscribe to use the app, I’ve lost all my historic data as a result of this and I won’t be forced paying £11 a month either to get it back.  Used to be an excellent app, the free version was brilliant and the paid subscription really expanded on it nicely of you needed the features. 
However the recent change to forcing everyone into subscription only has ruined it entirely, what made the app worthwhile has been entirely lost by this change and now it’s far below what would be expected from an app for this kind of things. Theres way better free apps that will do the same for you out there. Unless they change this forced subscription mode back to include the free option I suspect this will be the death of the app.

reviews.title: Very dissatisfied after years of loyalty
reviews.text:
Highly disappointed with the app’s sudden switch in subscription features, as a user who’s been using the app for the last 5 years. I no longer have access to the plates count feature which now sits behind a paywall (despite having recently renewed for another year). The least they could have done is to ensure longtime users are rewarded for their loyalty over these years by keeping these features accessible to them, rather than suddenly asking them to pay for a ‘pro’ plan to access features they’d always used on the lower level subscription plan.

I will be looking at alternative apps, and perhaps even look to build mine with AI. I’d recommend others do the same.

reviews.title: Used to be good, now disappointing
reviews.text:
I used this app for years and it used to be genuinely excellent — simple, flexible, and perfect for tracking strength training. Unfortunately, recent updates have turned it into a shadow of what it was.

The developer is clearly pushing hard toward a paid subscription, and the free/basic version has been stripped of essential functionality.

After years of loyalty, I’ve now found a much better replacement that offers flexibility without locking basic features behind a paywall. That says it all.

It’s a real shame to see such a solid app go this way.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
I paid for this app many years ago as a one off charge and have used it on and off ever since. 
Today I tried to open the app after taking a break over Christmas & NY only to be forced to provide a load of data like a new user and to buy a subscription (after a 7 day free trial) for an app I’d already paid for!

I understand that everything is now going subscription based for recurring revenue and I’ve had good use from the app for the amount I paid and the time I’ve used it, but surely you can’t just turn my account into a subscription when I’ve already paid when the subscription provides me with no more value than I had before. 

I tried to accept the 7 day free trial and use my email address to sign in to see if all my years of data is at least still there, but the app hangs with the spinning wheel of death, so I can’t even try it if I wanted to and all my history is presumably lost?

Nice way to look after your early adopters.

reviews.title: Brilliant App; Terrible Developer and Scamming business practices
reviews.text:
This app is great, I find it very intuitive with a pleasing design and UX. I’ve been using it on and off for years. So I decided to purchase the ‘Power Pack’ as a one off, lifetime purchase. The developer is now going out of their way to push everyone onto their new subscription. It doesn’t offer anything new or anything to benefit me. But every time I change screens in the app I get bombarded with full screen popups telling me to subscribe. 
I used to recommend this app to everyone, now I’m actively telling people to avoid it. Which is a great shame after supporting it for so long. 
I appreciate the costs of maintaining the app and you shouldn’t be punishing the people who supported you at the start of this journey.
Honour their purchases. Stop degrading the performance to get a few more subscriptions. You will push people, like me, off your app onto alternatives.
